subject: Discovery follow-up: fit validation action cards & rollback triggers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps: validation plan

Hi Elena / Sam —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same action items: 

Key takeaways
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + triage routing; tight correctness bar on entity extraction (esp. PII redaction)
- Volume profile: 300–800 qps during steady state, 1.2k bursts during peak
- Must-have: reproducible outputs for audit (retention + model snapshotting)

Proposed validation workstream (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Evaluation packet: benchmark suite (50k anonymized exchanges), prompt set, and automated scoring harness — bouncing this to the Drive folder after this email.
2) Recommended model shortlist: small latency candidate (gpt-like-open-7b-quant), accuracy candidate (redwood-rl-13b-finetuned), and fallback (gptx-3.5-compat). We’ll include throughput / latency profiles for 512-token and 1k-token tail.
3) Regression watchlist & rollback triggers: baseline metrics (F1 on named-entity set, hallucination rate on task prompts). We'll propose threshold-based triggers — e.g., >5% drop in entity F1 or >8% increase in hallucination rate triggers immediate mitigation.
4) Action cards: canary deploy plan, pin-to-snapshot option, and emergency rollback flow.

Attachments included: fidelis_eval_v1.2.pdf (summary), prompt_set_production.jsonl (anonymized prompts).

Next steps
- Jonas: lead the evaluation handoff and coordinate the initial run by end of next week.
- Rishi: prepare suggested quantization profiles and cost estimates.
- Elena/Sam: confirm the anonymized data upload to the Drive folder (I shared a folder link below).

If that all looks right I’ll schedule a short 30-min sync next Tues to walk the eval packet.

—Marissa

Thanks — this is great and mostly aligns with our expectations. Two points I want to call out before the sync:

1) Risk from last update: we observed a quality shift after your April runtime patch on a subset of canned prompts — shorter summaries started omitting critical PII markers. We need a concrete regression detection and fast rollback path.

2) Auditability: our compliance team will require a model snapshot and retained scoring logs for at least 90 days for any production change.

Can you include a short checklist of what constitutes a rollback trigger vs. what we’d accept as a degradable temporary variance? Also please add a proposed SLA for emergency rollback time (we’d like < 30 minutes from trigger detection to rollback in our critical flow).

—Elena

Elena — appreciate the flag and super helpful context. Below is an operational-first write-up that we’ll use as the canonical decision log for rollback vs tolerance. I’ve attached a short CSV of the April diff snapshots (diff-snapshots.zip) for preliminary review.

Operational criteria (short version)
- Regression trigger (requires immediate mitigation):
  * Entity F1 drop >= 5% absolute on the audit prompt set 
  * Hallucination rate increase >= 8% (measured by our hallucination binary check in the harness)
  * Any PII redaction misses that result in a confirmed compliance finding during manual sample review
- Degradable variance (monitor + canary):
  * Latency increase <= 20% with no accuracy drop
  * Small deviation in style/verbosity (<10% deviation on ROUGE-L)

Mitigation ladder (what we will do, in order)
1) Canary: divert 10% of traffic to previous snapshot (v20280412) and compare metrics live (5–15 minute window). If metrics recover to baseline, we expand to 50% and then full rollback.
2) Pin: if customer needs guaranteed reproducibility for a period, we pin traffic to a model snapshot (we’ll provide a pin token and snapshot ID).
3) Emergency rollback: slot swap on serving nodes — target < 30 minutes from detection to rollback completion for single-region deployments; multi-region adds propagation time (~15–30 mins extra).

What we’ll deliver by EOW:
- A one-page decision card (human readable) capturing the triggers above and how to execute each mitigation step. (I’ll draft and share by Monday morning.)
- An eval run using the attached prompt set; results will be uploaded to the Drive link and we’ll create a short Jira for automated alerting (INF-7321).
- A proposed SLA entry for rollback (<30 mins) to include as an appendix of the trial contract.

Technical notes for Rishi (internal)
- Please include a quick-cost delta for running pinned snapshots for 30/90 days and the estimated GPU capacity required for a 10% canary at their projected qps.
- Share recommended quantization profiles and whether the latency candidate can meet their 300–800 qps target at 512 tokens.

Elena — does that structure work for you for the initial contract appendix? Happy to jump on the sync if you want to step through the decision card live.

—Jonas
